I rarely need to see a doctor, but I do have a primary care physician whom I check in with once a year just to make sure I"m good. Recently my primary care moved locations, making it a 2-hour round trip to see him, so I switched doctors.

A few days ago I went to my new doctor and decided to ask him for advice on quitting smoking. (I know, I know, judge all you want, I have no excuses) We talked about nicotine patches, but then he started asking me questions about my weight. For the record I have a BMI of 18.6. I weigh myself every morning just to make sure I'm maintaining and I am very careful about what I eat. I am petite and only need around 1400 calories each day, so every calorie counts, would rather kill myself than be fat, etc.

So I really like this doctor, but not what he had to say next. First he asks me, "How do you feel about your body now?". I said I felt great, had no physical complaints, love being active, sick of knowing that I'm hastening my own death by smoking, etc. Then he starts talking about how nicotine is an appetite suppressant and that even though it is extremely important that I quit smoking, I should be prepared for the inevitable weight gain. He says, "You could stand to gain a few pounds anyway, you are underweight.". I said, "No, if I lost a few pounds I would be underweight, but I maintain my weight very strictly so that won't be a problem."

He continues on that line of reasoning anyway. He says he just wanted to warn me because he didn't want me to become discouraged and go back to smoking just because I might gain a little weight. I just said, "Why would I gain weight if I don't change my eating habits? I mean, I understand that it may be more of a challenge, but weight gain will not be inevitable because I won't eat more than I need even if not smoking makes that more difficult, at least at first." He says, "Don't be overconfident and sabotage yourself.".

Sigh. I get where he is coming from, I really do, but honestly I overcame alcoholism, I kind of have an idea of what I'm in for. But I'm willing to do it because I'm not willing to continue being a fucking idiot with my health. It's just discouraging when even doctors don't know what they're talking about when it comes to weight gain.
Doc tells me to beware of the inevitable weight gain I will experience when quitting smoking.

I am a smoker myself and if I don't smoke for a while, I feel like eating more...it doesn't mean though that I should start devouring meal after meal :) I remember reading another study (unfortunately I cannot find you a link to it right now), that claimed that your TDEE will decrease with 200-400 calories after quitting because of the metabolic effects of nicotine. Cheap & Easy Homemade Jerky - No Dehydrator Needed

This easy & cheap homemade turkey jerky recipe requires only a conventional oven but you can still use a dehydrator if you happen to have one! Jerky in general is a great high protein snack option for road trips, hiking, or school/work. Unfortunately many store bought jerkies are quite expensive and packed with chemicals and added sugar. This homemade turkey jerky is easy to make and a lot cheaper & healthier than store bought counterparts. You can also use beef or pork for this recipe if turkey is a bit expensive in your area.

Calorie and macro information per serving (2 servings total):

133 calories, 2F, 1C, 1 sugar, 24P

Recipe:

Ingredients:

  • 200 g turkey breast (thinly sliced into long strips)
  • 1 Tbsp light soy sauce
  • 1 Tbsp cheap red dry wine
  • 1 tsp chili paste
  • .25 tsp garlic powder
  • .25 tsp red pepper flakes (or less)

Equipment needed:

  • Skewers
  • Al foil
  • Plastic wrap
  • Conventional oven or dehydrator
  • Fridge

Instructions:

  1. Add in soy sauce, red wine, chili paste, garlic powder, and red pepper flakes into a large mixing bowl.

  2. Add in turkey breast strips and mix very well. Cover with plastic wrap and marinade for 6 to 12 hours.

  3. After 6 to 12 hours preheat the oven to 165˚F or 74˚C. Use skewers to hang all of the turkey breast strips. 3 to 4 pieces per skewer.

  4. Line the bottom of the oven with Al foil to catch any grease or marinade. Use the oven metal rack to hang all of the skewers and leave a few inches apart. Cook in the oven for 4 hours or until the turkey meat is completely dry.

Optional: if you have a dehydrator then you can lay the turkey breast in the dehydrator until the meats are dry.

For beef you can use 142˚F or 62˚C and for pork you can use 145˚F or 63˚C.

  1. You can serve this right away or you can store them in a ziplock bag for later. If the meats are completely dry, you can store in an airtight container for a few months.

Enjoy!
